title: Db stuck and unresponsive
body:
### To reproduce

I haven't specific steps to reproduce that but today we received a lot of errors from ours productions app due to db not reachable.
It is completely stuck (it's the second time in a more or less a week), I attached the full container log.

The only thing we do every day, except for Sunday, is a database restart in order to backup the Hyper-V environment. In our case Hyper-V host the Ubuntu VM that runs QuestDb using Docker on ZFS.
All the VMs are shutdown gracefully before backup.

### QuestDB version:

8.2.1

### OS, in case of Docker specify Docker and the Host OS:

Ubuntu 22.04 (Docker)

### File System, in case of Docker specify Host File System:

ZFS

### Full Name:

Enrico Benedos

### Affiliation:

Deimos

### Have you followed Linux, MacOs kernel configuration steps to increase Maximum open files and Maximum virtual memory areas limit?

- [X] Yes, I have

### Additional context

[xam.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18226540/xam.zip)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/37f8dad8-59fa-45d9-9dca-4d32b3afa6de)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: It seems the column file is broken. There are already some issues reported on Windows docker by other users: https://github.com/questdb/questdb/issues/4969. They were ok to run windows native binaries. Perhaps you can run native windows binaries?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Sorry @participant1, what do you mean with 

> Perhaps you can run native windows binaries?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> Sorry @participant1, what do you mean with
> 
> > Perhaps you can run native windows binaries?

Instead of running QuestDB in Docker on Windows, you can try running the QuestDB Windows binary directly. There is a tutorial available [here](https://questdb.com/docs/quick-start/#binaries).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: But I'm not running on Windows, as you can see on the issue creation text.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> But I'm not running on Windows, as you can see on the issue creation text.

Hey reporter. I noticed that you are running an Ubuntu VM on Hyper-V (Windows) as your Docker run environment. I'm not sure if this will have an impact, but there have been precedents of failing to run Docker containers directly on Windows with similar exceptions. You might want to try running the binary directly on Windows.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: By me it hasn't so much sense. The environment/host is Ubuntu, there is no Windows to get considered.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
Hey @reporter we are not guessing here. The setup you have is simply not something we tested on. There are bugs, quirks in each layer that simply creates unfathomable combinatorial problem.

Our recommended and supported setup is Linux, specifically Ubuntu and redhat is where we tested. Including running docker on top of them.

Please consider moving to a supported software stack. We are happy to validate your configuration before you commit to it.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hi @participant2, what is for you a supported software stack? I don't think that buy a dedicated hardware only for Quest is a good way to manage a 2025 stack.

by me considering the virtualizer an adjunctive layer is an error, at least in this normal case. All the world is based on an hardware with a virtualizer (Hyper-V, VmWare, ProxMox, Kvm, etc..). 
In the real life anyone using a on-premise stack is using a virtualizer. Also the cloud environments are using virtualizer in the background, so for example if you are delivering your service in Azure it probably runs on a Hyper-V VM in a Docker instance.

I specified Hyper-V only for accuracy, but it is a normal Ubuntu with Docker with ZFS. 

I think that the problem is ZFS or something in that area, probably the database it's not really ready to support ZFS backups/snapshots (that's a bit weird). 

We have Mongo, Postgres and SqlServer instances that runs without any issue with a lot of data and opened connections. At this point we probably rely on something else.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
We have big production environments running on Azure with ZFS without issues.  We have no idea what you're doing and we cannot go on an expedition of looking for we don't know what from the description you provided.

If you can build a reproducer for us, we will debug, otherwise everything we're discussing here is a speculation.

If you want to use something else - absolutely for go for it.

So the exact queries which were running fine earlier, now giving "Some error occurred, Try after some time" OR  "Quest DB not reachable error". Is there any change in the query structure, in new version. Or what might be the reason??

- share query text
- share logs

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
@participant2 Yeah, sure. This is the query
```

WITH vehicle_groups AS (
        SELECT
            15 AS vehicle_id,
            'FORK_LIFT_1' as vehicle_type,
            20 AS max_speed_threshold,
            12 AS min_speed_threshold
),

flattened_vehicle_data AS (
    -- First flatten all vehicle data to handle v1_id and v2_id separately
    SELECT
        nm.v1_id AS vehicle_id,
        nm.duration,
        nm.type,
        nm.speed,
        nm.min_distance,
        nm.timestamp,
        nm.x,
        nm.y,
        vg.min_speed_threshold as min_speed_threshold,
        vg.max_speed_threshold as max_speed_threshold
    FROM near_misses nm
    LEFT JOIN vehicle_groups vg ON CAST(nm.v1_id AS INT) = vg.vehicle_id
    WHERE nm.v1_id IN (15)
      AND nm.timestamp BETWEEN '2025-07-22T00:00:00.000Z' AND '2025-07-23T17:42:38.952Z'

    UNION ALL

    SELECT
        nm.v2_id AS vehicle_id,
        nm.duration,
        nm.type,
        nm.speed,
        nm.min_distance,
        nm.timestamp,
        nm.x,
        nm.y,
        vg.min_speed_threshold as min_speed_threshold,
        vg.max_speed_threshold as max_speed_threshold
    FROM near_misses nm
    LEFT JOIN vehicle_groups vg ON CAST(nm.v2_id AS INT) = vg.vehicle_id
    WHERE nm.v2_id IN (15)
      AND nm.timestamp BETWEEN '2025-06-24T00:00:00.000Z' AND '2025-07-23T17:42:38.952Z'
)
SELECT * FROM flattened_vehicle_data;
```

And the error it gave was

**"QuestDB is not reachable[500]"**


After removing some columns from the SELECT statement and using the actual table name 'near_miss' instead of the alias 'nm', it worked correctly.
